children: Russian ruble wheat prices rose for a second week, largely on slower farmer selling as the need to raise working capital eased, grains consultancy SovEcon says in a note. Export demand is also helping. The firm estimates Russia's October wheat exports at 2.8 million metric tons, up from 2.1 million tons in August on stronger shipments through the Baltic Sea. Government plans to buy 3 million tons of grain between Nov. 1 and June 30 may have provided some support, although the impact should be limited as constraints on Black Sea exports leave Russia roughly 2 million to 3 million tons per month short of normal export volumes, SovEcon adds. CBOT wheat futures are off 1.3%. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
